title: Week 4 POC: Readiness Handoff and Benchmark Interpretation
summary: Quick weekly sync to review the POC benchmark numbers, confirm access for the Dedicated pilot nodes, discuss observed latency regressions on longer contexts, and agree on immediate handoff tasks to move to customer-managed staging. Action items include sharing the annotated benchmark spreadsheet, opening a peering ticket, and scheduling an on-prem handshake call with infra team.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-03 15:30 PT | Duration 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Morales (Redwood SE), Diane Park (Novato Health - Head of ML), Samir Patel (Novato - Platform), Laura Gomez (Novato - Security)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda: benchmark recap, access handoff, and tuning notes. is that still what people want to focus on?
[00:06] Diane: yeah that's fine, i mostly want to understand the numbers you ran on the 4k sequences, and it's been a bit noisy on our side so hoping for clarity.
[00:12] Ethan: cool, i'll walk through the runbook and the spreadsheet we shared, and call out anomalies.
[00:18] Samir: and from infra we care about the VPC peering, certs, and whether we need to adjust our NAT gateway route.
[00:24] Laura: security will need the audit log cadence and confirmation about key rotation - is that covered?
[00:30] Maya: yes, we'll touch on audit logs and KMS integration. okay ethan, over to you for the numbers.

[00:45] Ethan: alright so, quick reminder: we ran three workload shapes - small chat 256 tokens, mid 1k, and long 4k context. test runs were on Redwood Dedicated standard GPU pool, quantized runtime 4-bit that we matched to the model variant you selected. the sheet has per-call p50/p95 for token latency and token cost.
[01:10] Diane: can you call out the p95 for the 4k? that's where we saw regressions.
[01:15] Ethan: sure. p95 for 4k was about 2.9s per token in our env, which translates to about 18s tail for the final 64 tokens chunk, so it does spike. we think it's related to KV cache evictions on our batching strategy when sequence lengths vary a lot.
[01:40] Samir: kv cache evictions... do you mean K-V as in key-value or some other cache? i've seen that term in your docs but it's spelled differently in our tickets.
[01:47] Ethan: yeah some transcripts autocorrect to K-V cache, but it's the runtime's KV cache for attention states. when batches mix short and very long requests the cache gets churn and causes extra IO.
[02:05] Diane: is there a config we can change short-term? we can't run with that tail on production.
[02:10] Ethan: two levers: you can pin requests into homogeneous queues (i.e. separate routes for long context), or we can tune continuous batching thresholds so long requests bypass batching when they exceed X tokens. for the POC we recommend route-based segregation since it's simple.

[02:38] Maya: note for the team's planning: segregating routes will increase call counts and might affect cost modeling, so we'll share a cost delta.
[02:46] Ethan: i already added a separate sheet that models cost per 10k requests if you separate long-context traffic; it's in the shared spreadsheet link (see notes).

[03:05] Laura: on the security side, how are audit logs surfaced? we need both token-level cost anonymized logs and full request/response logs for debugging but with PII redaction.
[03:16] Maya: Redwood can stream audit logs to your Splunk or S3 with redaction hooks. for POC we propose S3 with lifecycle 90 days, and you can configure redaction rules.
[03:28] Laura: ok, can we get an example of the redaction rule set?
[03:31] Ethan: yes we'll paste our standard redaction policy, but note the redaction is regex based and sometimes over-redacts, so we'll work with your security team to iterate.

[03:50] Diane: back to the benchmarks — i see two outlier runs on the morning of 6/1 where the p95 jumps. any idea what caused that?
[03:58] Ethan: we correlate those with multi-tenant noise on the Dedicated nodes we were using for a few hours; the nodes were under higher background system load due to another customer's burst. that should not happen for your reserved Dedicated pool once provisioned.
[04:18] Samir: so the Dedicated pool you're testing on today was not isolated? i thought Dedicated meant reserved.
[04:23] Ethan: this was a pre-provisioned sandbox of Dedicated; it had some burst isolation but not absolute. your Dedicated contract will be isolated. we'll highlight which numbers came from the sandbox vs fully isolated pool.

[04:40] Maya: i'll flag that in the annotated sheet.

[04:48] Diane: what's the expected SLO once we're on reserved capacity? p95 for 1k under 600ms is our target.
[04:55] Ethan: from our verified profiles, 1k p95 on reserved standard pool is around 420-500ms depending on batching. we can push latency down further with priority lanes and lower batching but that will increase cost.

[05:15] Samir: discuss access handoff — we've got a ticket in our system for VPC peering but we need the exact CIDR ranges and cert fingerprints.
[05:23] Maya: we sent an infra checklist earlier; i can re-share. cidrs, peer ASN, and the service endpoint are in that doc. for certs, we'll generate a short-lived TLS cert for the test window and rotate on handoff.
[05:36] Samir: can you put the cert fingerprint in the ticket so we can validate?
[05:39] Ethan: yes will do.

[05:50] Laura: also want assurance on KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[05:56] Maya: yes we support customer-managed KMS in the Private deployment and with Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS. HSM integrations require enterprise lane but can be arranged. we'll add the KMS integration diagram to the security packet.

[06:20] Diane: one more benchmark question: the token generation quality looked slightly different between quantized run and fp16 run. is that expected?
[06:29] Ethan: yes there's often small distributional shifts with 4-bit quantization. for most prompts it's negligible but for some safety or rare token cases there can be divergence. that's why we recommend eval prompt sets to catch regressions — we can run a targeted eval against your prompt-suite.
[06:50] Diane: please run that against our 200 prompt set. we'll share the set after the call.

[07:00] Maya: logging a next step: run quality eval against Novato's 200 prompt set.

[07:08] Samir: timeline questions — we're aiming to move into customer-managed staging by mid-June. is that realistic?
[07:13] Ethan: probably yes if we get VPC peering and credentials this week. provisioning takes 48 hours once we have PEER details and the contract items are signed.

[07:25] Laura: we need SOC2 artifacts and your penetration test summary before we sign the staging contract.
[07:31] Maya: we'll send SOC2 summary, pen test redline, and the compliance packet within 24 hours.

[07:40] Diane: any known issues with our infra stack — we're on EKS with NAT gateway and a private NLB.
[07:46] Ethan: that's a supported topology. the one note: if you use a private NLB you need exact health check paths and ensure the NLB outbound rules allow our egress to the control plane. i'll paste an example NLB rule set.

[08:05] Samir: ok we'll review.

[08:10] Ethan: some quick tuning notes we recommend: set batching window to 30ms for chat workloads, separate long-context route that disables batching, and use a small KV cache TTL bump when you have repeated prompt prefixes. these are low-risk changes.

[08:28] Diane: curious about cost — if we separate routes, what's the step function for cost vs latency?
[08:35] Ethan: i sketched it in the sheet: segregating long requests increases per-request cost about 8-12% but reduces p95 tail by ~30% on heavy long-context mixes. the tradeoff depends on ratio of long to short requests.

[09:00] Maya: okay let's go through action items now.
[09:05] Ethan: first, i'll annotate the benchmark sheet rows that came from sandbox versus isolated nodes.
[09:10] Ethan: second, run the eval on the 200 prompt set once you share it, and produce a small regression report.
[09:18] Maya: third, i'll re-share the infra checklist and KMS diagram and the SOC2/pen test pack.
[09:24] Samir: fourth, i'll open the peering ticket and attach the CIDR and logs we need.
[09:29] Laura: fifth, we'll review redaction rules and send a pointer doc back by Friday.
[09:34] Diane: sixth, schedule the on-prem handshake with our infra team next Tuesday — is that possible?
[09:39] Maya: yes, tuesday 6/9 works for us, i'll propose a time in the invite.

[09:48] Ethan: quick note: we noticed one reproducible regression when context concatenation with system prompt exceeded 6k tokens. we suggest a guardrail in your client to drop system prompt for extremely long sessions until we enable progressive KV streaming.
[10:10] Diane: understood — we'll implement a client-side guardrail as interim.

[10:18] Samir: any blockers from Redwood side?
[10:21] Maya: nothing blocking. we need the prompt set and VPC details this week to keep mid-June target.

[10:30] Laura: one last compliance Q: do you provide TLS mutual auth for internal control-plane connections?
[10:35] Ethan: mutual TLS can be enabled on Private installs; for Dedicated we support token-based mutual auth and can arrange mTLS for an enterprise contract. we'll include options.

[10:50] Maya: great, recap: maya to send security packet and cidr examples, ethan to annotate benchmarks and run evals, samir to open peering ticket, diane to share prompts, laura to draft redaction rules. propose next sync same time next week unless we need an earlier triage.
[11:12] Diane: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:18] Maya: thanks, bye.
